prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas. Injury: back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1376; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record for this exercise. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Fine. Let's go with that. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving on a multi-lane road in Baytown, Texas, heading toward the east side of town during the late afternoon.

Q: Walk me through what happened right before the impact.
A: I was in the right lane and I was about to move into the middle lane to get around a slow delivery van. I checked my mirror, I saw a gap, and I signaled. As I started to drift over, a sedan in the middle lane came up beside me and its side clipped the front passenger side of my vehicle.

Q: Did you see the sedan before you began to change lanes?
A: I saw it in my mirror, but it looked like it was behind me by a good distance. It closed the gap faster than I expected.

Q: After the contact, what did you do?
A: I gripped the wheel and steered back to the right lane. I pulled onto the shoulder and turned on my hazard lights. The other driver stopped a little ahead of me.

Q: Did you feel any pain at the scene?
A: Not right away. I felt a tightness in my lower back that got worse over the next few hours, especially when I tried to get out of the car.

Q: What treatment have you received for your back?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same evening, and they took X-rays and told me it was a muscle strain. They gave me medication and told me to rest and use ice. I later started physical therapy twice a week at a clinic near my home.

Q: Are you still attending physical therapy?
A: Yes, though the sessions are less frequent now. My therapist has me doing stretches at home every morning and evening.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: I have trouble lifting anything heavy, including groceries and laundry baskets. I can't sit for long periods without my back aching, so I've had to stand during meals and rest often at work. I used to coach my son's weekend soccer team, and I've had to hand that over to my wife for now.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I missed a few days in the first weeks, and since then I've been on modified duties that keep me from lifting more than a few pounds.

Q: Is there anything else you want to add about how this has affected you?
A: Mostly I just want to get back to normal. Some mornings I can barely bend to tie my shoes, and that's frustrating for someone who used to be active every day.
